title: Preparing for death
hookLine: a will, wishes, reconciliations made in time
tomorrow: call the priest now, or wait till the very end? who's right?

lines: NOBODY WANTS TO BRING UP THE WILL.
cards: Nobody wants to be the one at a family dinner who brings up the will. But grandmothers say it, lawyers say it, and so does a prophet: put your house in order.
Isaiah walks in on a sick king, Hezekiah, and says, in the Douay-Rheims Bible: "Take order with thy house, for thou shalt die, and not live." Then the strange part. The king doesn't die.
He turns his face to the wall, prays and weeps, and God answers: I will add to thy days fifteen years. So what was the order for?

teach.b: Here's the puzzle solved: the order wasn't wasted, because it was never only about the date. Setting a house in order is good for the living. Catholics talk about preparing for death as love made practical.
A will, so the family isn't left fighting over a kitchen table.

teach.h: A WILL, WISHES, A CALL MADE.
teach.b: Wishes written down: which parish, which song, whether to call a priest for the anointing. And reconciliations made in time: the call to the brother you stopped speaking to, the apology that's been waiting.
In the old Litany of the Saints, Catholics asked God to spare them a sudden and unprepared death.
Something to tell a friend tonight: the fear in that prayer isn't dying. It's dying without the chance to get ready. Hezekiah got his chance, and then more years to live inside it.
It lets you face whatever comes with less left undone, and that's what prepare in peace means.

how: Catholics prepare for death by making a will and an advance directive, telling family their wishes for the sacraments and the funeral, going to confession, and seeking reconciliation; parishes and Catholic health systems often help with end-of-life planning.

giving up on treatment and waiting

games.why: Hezekiah was told to set his house in order and then lived on. the order wasn't wasted: prepare in peace.

practice: On a piece of paper, write one wish for the end of your life, whenever it comes: a song, a person you'd want near, a prayer, something you'd want said or settled. Just one.
Fold it, keep it where you'll find it, and let the sit be quiet around it.

wordCard.voice: Preparing for death. Setting your house in order, a will, wishes, peace made, so the people you love aren't left guessing.

orig.note: Latin, Isaiah 38:1 in the Vulgate: set your house in order.

carryVoice: Hold onto this: prepare in peace, the way Hezekiah set his house in order and then lived on. See you tomorrow.
